text: gemma.ai is Google DeepMind's Gemma documentation site: its pages are titled '… - Gemma Documentation' and end with 'Copyright © 2026 Google DeepMind'; the ai.google.dev/gemma/docs pages the reference cites (prompt-formatting-gemma4, mtp/mtp) still resolve on 2026-10-15, and the Gemma 4 prompt-formatting text is the same on both sites apart from layout and gemma.ai's added Gemma 1-3 section.

Note: <|tool_response> acts as an additional stop sequence for the inference engine.

text: gemma.ai's releases page dates Gemma 4 in E2B, E4B, 31B and 26B A4B to March 31, 2026, the MTP drafters for those four sizes to April 16, 2026, Gemma 4 12B Unified to June 3, 2026 and EmbeddingGemma 2 to October 6, 2026; no later Gemma release is listed on 2026-10-15.

sources.quote: April 16, 2026 Release of Gemma 4 - MTP for E2B, E4B, 31B, and 26B A4B.

text: Google's gemma.ai LiteRT-LM page says LiteRT-LM's MTP speeds up decoding 'with no quality loss: up to 2.2x on mobile GPUs and 1.5x on mobile CPUs', without naming devices, files or dates, and recommends MTP for every task on GPU backends and for E4B on CPU, and selectively for E2B on CPU, where it can slow freeform generation slightly.

sources.quote: LiteRT-LM supports MTP, which speeds up decoding with no quality loss: up to 2.2x on mobile GPUs and 1.5x on mobile CPUs.
Google recommends MTP for every task on GPU backends, and for E4B on CPU.

text: gemma.ai's LiteRT-LM page gives .litertlm bundle sizes of 2.58 GB (E2B) and 3.65 GB (E4B), which are the litert-community cards' 'Model size' figures (2,583 and 3,654 MB) in GB; the pinned plain files are 2,588,147,712 and 3,659,530,240 bytes, so the page's figures are a little below the files' sizes, and the page says LiteRT-LM ships E2B and E4B 'with larger models coming'.

sources.quote: LiteRT-LM ships E2B and E4B, with larger models coming.

formula: 2,588,147,712 B = 2.588 GB; 3,659,530,240 B = 3.660 GB (decimal); the page's 2.58 and 3.65 match the cards' 2,583 and 3,654 MB (MOD-FAM-046)

text: gemma.ai's LiteRT-LM page documents exporting a Hugging Face Gemma 4 checkpoint (fine-tuned or not) to .litertlm with the litert-torch-nightly package: 'litert-torch export_hf --model=google/gemma-4-E2B-it' with --externalize_embedder and --jinja_chat_template_override=litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm, which takes the chat template from the litert-community repository.

sources.quote: Export Safetensors — including a model you have fine-tuned — to the .litertlm format: uv tool install litert-torch-nightly litert-torch export_hf

text: gemma.ai's MTP page says Gemma 4's drafter (the 'lightweight 4-layer MTP drafter') gives speedups 'while guaranteeing the exact same quality as standard autoregressive generation', and shows it only with Hugging Face Transformers and do_sample=False; gemma.ai's MTP visual guide, reposted from Exploring Language Models, says 'similar quality' instead.

sources.quote: This results in significant decoding speedups while guaranteeing the exact same quality as standard autoregressive generation
These enhancements result in significant decoding speedups while guaranteeing similar quality

text: gemma.ai's function-calling page runs google/gemma-4-E2B-it with Hugging Face Transformers and its Hugging Face chat template and shows the model's tool-call output ending '<tool_call|><|tool_response>', that is with stop token 50; it shows no E4B output and nothing about LiteRT-LM or the .litertlm file's template.

gemma.ai's 'A Visual Guide to Gemma 4' (reposted from Exploring Language Models) lists K=V among changes that relate to all model sizes and says local layers have 2 query heads per KV head and global layers 8; neither holds for E2B or E4B, whose pinned configs set attention_k_eq_v false, 8 query heads on 1 (E2B) or 2 (E4B) KV heads in every layer, and no num_global_key_value_heads.

sources.quote: The local attention layers use GQA and have 2 Query heads sharing one KV head.
There are a number of things that were changed compared to Gemma 3 that relate to all model sizes:

sources.detail: text_config rows attention_k_eq_v, num_attention_heads, num_key_value_heads, num_global_key_value_heads for gemma-4-E2B-it and gemma-4-E4B-it

conflicts_with: gemma.ai visual guide: K=V for all sizes; 2:1 local and 8:1 global query-to-KV grouping

text: gemma.ai's QAT page says the E2B and E4B '-qat-mobile-transformers' and '-qat-mobile-ct' checkpoints use a custom wNa8o8 scheme 'with 2-bit decoding layers and optimized KV caches'; it does not say whether the litert-community .litertlm files are built from them.

sources.quote: -mobile-* weights are built on a custom wNa8o8 schema with 2-bit decoding layers and optimized KV caches
